title: The believer in Pharaoh's house
hookLine: a man of Pharaoh's family who hid his faith speaks up for Musa (40:28)

lines: A VOICE FROM INSIDE THE CIRCLE.
cards: Pharaoh's court. The decision is nearly made. Pharaoh says: let me kill Musa, and let him call on his Lord.
I'm afraid he'll change your religion, or spread corruption in the land. The advisers nod. It's the kind of room where disagreeing could cost you everything.

Then a voice speaks up from inside the circle. Not an outsider, not one of Musa's people: a member of Pharaoh's own family, who has kept his faith hidden for who knows how long. Today, he can't keep quiet anymore.

teach.h: A BELIEVER WHO HID HIS FAITH.
WOULD YOU KILL A MAN FOR THIS?
teach.b: Pickthall: "And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah". This is why some call the surah Al-Mu'min, the Believer. He's never named.
Listen to how carefully he argues. He doesn't announce his faith; he asks a question. Then he reasons with them on their own terms.
If Musa is lying, his lie is on him. If he's telling the truth, some of what he warns you about will reach you. You lose nothing by leaving him alone.
He's not grandstanding. He's trying to save a life in a room that doesn't want to hear it. And he keeps going, over many verses.
He reminds them of nations destroyed before them, and of Yusuf, who came to Egypt long before and was doubted too. He calls them to salvation while they call him to the fire.

teach.h: I ENTRUST MY AFFAIR TO ALLAH.
teach.b: Finally, verse forty-four: you'll remember what I'm telling you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Verse forty-five: so Allah protected him from the evils they plotted.
A moment in the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ echoes this.

Bukhari reports that when a man in Mecca attacked him as he prayed and began to choke him, Abu Bakr pushed the man away and said these same words: would you kill a man because he says my Lord is Allah?
One voice, inside the room, can be enough to stop the room.

how: Muslim teachers often cite the believer of Pharaoh's family as an example of wise, courageous speech, and many recite his words 'I entrust my affair to Allah' (40:44) in times of fear.

o: the Forgiver; the surah's other name is the Believer
the name of the hidden believer in Pharaoh's court
a title for Musa as the one who forgave Egypt

games.q: the believer in Pharaoh's house — tap the pairs.
p: would you kill a man for this?
I entrust my affair to Allah
said the same words in Mecca

s: the Qur'an gives the believer's name
he's never named; the text calls him a believing man of Pharaoh's family.
he argued that if Musa lied, the lie was on Musa alone
if he's lying, his lie is on him; if true, you're at risk.
Allah protected him from what they plotted
verse forty-five says so, after he entrusted his affair to Allah.

games.q: you're a member of Pharaoh's family, secretly a believer. Pharaoh wants Musa dead. what do you do?
o: ask: would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah?
games.why: he spoke up with a careful question and reasoned with them, and later entrusted his affair to Allah, who protected him.

practice: Think of a room you're often in, a team, a family chat, a group of friends, where someone gets talked about unfairly. Picture yourself saying one calm sentence for them, not a speech, a question like his: is that really fair?
Then entrust the rest, to God if you pray, or simply let it go.

wordCard.voice: Ghafir, the Forgiver, the surah also called Al-Mu'min, where an unnamed believer in Pharaoh's own family spoke up to save Musa. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a believing man, which gives the surah its other name, Al-Mu'min.

carryVoice: Your line: one voice inside. The Qur'an never names him; it keeps his question. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3678 (Abu Bakr defends the Prophet with 40:28)
